name: What should be done before demolition starts?

mainEntity.name: What prep steps should happen before a gut renovation demolition crew arrives?
mainEntity.text: What prep steps should happen before a gut renovation demolition crew arrives?

acceptedAnswer.text: Good demolition prep prevents expensive mistakes. Before the crew starts, the project should have approved plans, permit approvals or active permit status, clear scope documents, and a decision on what stays and what goes. The homeowner should remove furniture, valuables, and fragile items; arrange utility coordination; protect floors or areas that remain; confirm dumpster placement; and verify any testing needed for hazardous materials. It is also smart to document the existing condition with photos in case there are questions later. If the project includes a kitchen or bathroom shutdown, plan temporary living arrangements and storage in advance. The more complete the prep, the faster demolition can move and the less likely the team is to damage items that were meant to be saved.
acceptedAnswer.description: Before demolition starts, the homeowner should finalize plans, secure permits, remove personal belongings, shut off or coordinate utilities, protect items that will remain, confirm dumpster access, and verify hazardous-material testing. Good preparation reduces delays, damage, and confusion once the site opens up.
